title: Stop Your Automation Sending the Same Message Twice
rights: Original educational script and graphics created for RMC AI Workshop/APEX. Locally generated CMU Flite slt narration. No third-party photographs, music, or footage.
description: A practical duplicate-prevention checklist for small-business automation. Use a stable event ID, persist the delivery result, and reconcile an uncertain outcome before retrying. Demonstration only: no customer messages are sent. Synthetic narration. This workflow improves reliability; it does not guarantee sales or exactly-once delivery across every provider.

scenes.heading: One request. Two messages?
scenes.text: A timeout can hide a successful send.
scenes.narration: Your automation sends a customer reply, then the connection drops. Did the send fail, or only the confirmation? Retrying blindly can send the same message twice.

scenes.heading: 1. Name the event
scenes.narration: Give the original request a stable event ID. Keep that same ID through retries. A new timestamp on every attempt makes one request look like several different jobs.

scenes.heading: 2. Store the attempt
scenes.narration: Before sending, record the event ID, intended destination, and action in persistent storage. A database unique constraint can stop two workers from claiming the same action at once.

scenes.heading: 3. Use provider protection
scenes.text: Pass the same idempotency key when supported.
scenes.narration: If your sending provider supports an idempotency key, pass the same key on every retry. Check its documentation for key lifetime and scope. Not every provider offers this protection.

scenes.heading: 4. Keep the receipt
scenes.text: Store the provider message ID and result.
scenes.narration: After success, save the provider message ID and mark the action complete. On restart, check that durable record before doing the work again. A memory-only list will disappear.

scenes.heading: 5. Treat unknown as unknown
scenes.text: Reconcile before retrying an uncertain send.
scenes.narration: If a timeout leaves the outcome uncertain, check the provider record before retrying. Without a receipt or provider protection, park the job for investigation instead of guessing.

scenes.heading: Test the awkward cases
scenes.narration: Test with fictional requests: submit a duplicate, interrupt a send, and restart the worker. Confirm one intended delivery. Follow RMC AI Workshop for practical automation lessons.
